evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Scope and behavior are concrete (create game with name/optional description); a reasonable implementation estimate can be made without detailed design.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Functional requirement is specific (generate/provide URL for invitations); estimatable at implementation level.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Clear UI interaction and outcome; scope is sufficiently bounded to estimate effort.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Requirement to display session items is concrete and can be estimated (list view, retrieval).

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item to show for estimation is specific UI behavior and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item to a list is a bounded feature (form, storage) and can be reasonably estimated.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item is a concrete operation (UI + persistence) and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Delete operation is well scoped and can be estimated (confirmation, removal).

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Behavior (show estimates immediately even if not all estimators have given their estimate) is concrete and implementable, allowing estimation.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting the average is a clearly specified action (compute average, accept), so it is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Trigger condition and outcome are defined; implementing automatic fill is specific enough to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Manually entering the agreed estimate is straightforward and bounded, allowing estimation.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimation behavior is clear (select prior story, allow new estimate) and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing from spreadsheets is a concrete integration task; implementation choices (formats) can be decided during planning without requiring detailed design to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste support is a narrow UI/UX feature with bounded scope and estimatable effort.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing historical games (list/detail view) is concrete and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Providing a transcript view is a clear deliverable (formatting and retrieval) and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting to HTML is a specific output format and is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Export to CSV is concrete and can be estimated (field mapping, CSV generation).

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Delete game semantics are clear (remove game and associated data); estimatable implementation work.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Account creation with specified fields is concrete and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Authentication flow is a well-defined feature and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Updating account details is a bounded feature (UI + persistence) and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion with cascade of games/data is specific enough to estimate (though edge cases exist, scope is bounded).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display behavior is concrete and implementable, allowing reasonable estimation.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder via email is a well-scoped feature (email flow) and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Choice between two explicitly enumerated card sets is specific and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: A clear numeric limit (15) bounds the feature; effort to enforce/handle is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via URL with name entry is concrete and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Displaying the current item is a specific UI behavior with bounded implementation effort.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Displaying the session backlog is concrete and estimatable (list retrieval and UI).

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Indicating per-estimator submission status is specific and implementable; estimatable effort.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Behavior is well-defined (show after all submitted) and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Permission to change estimate with a clear stopping condition is specific and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Displaying historical estimates for the same story is a bounded feature (history retrieval + display) and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Displaying who's given which estimate in current round is concrete and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Timer duration and shared visibility are explicit; implementation effort is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Reset condition and timer behavior are specific and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Providing scroll/navigation of prior rounds is a concrete UI/UX feature and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Requirement to maintain card order is specific and implementable; estimatable effort.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Clear rule for when estimate changes are allowed; scope is bounded and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail near card play is a concrete UI task with estimatable effort.

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Target standards are named (XHTML/CSS) so work can be scoped and estimated; although cross-cutting, it's estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Creating a glossary is a bounded deliverable (document + UI) and can be estimated without detailed design.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: 'as fast as possible' is an unbounded, vague performance target; scope depends on unknown queries and data, so a reasonable estimate cannot be made from this wording alone.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Supported browser versions are explicitly listed, so compatibility effort can be scoped and estimated.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Target (W3C accessibility guidelines) is named; while 'where possible' leaves some discretion, the intent and standard provide sufficient scope to estimate implementation effort.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Term 'respond quickly' is subjective and unspecific (no measurable performance target), making reasonable implementation estimation infeasible.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Supporting Unicode is a concrete technical requirement (character encoding support) and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design expectation is qualitative but implementable (define route patterns); estimatable scope for routing/URLs.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Creating user-friendly error pages is a bounded UI task; although 'nice' is subjective, the work is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: 'Non-identifiable' is ambiguous/legalistic and lacks specification of anonymization/de-identification methods and requirements, preventing a reliable implementation estimate.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Phrase 'some metrics' is vague and does not specify which metrics or granularity; scope is underspecified, so effort cannot be reliably estimated.
